steps.do: Start the Vite dev server that serves the modal demo page.
Run the responsive Playwright spec that opens the modal at 320 by 568 pixels.
Confirm the spec asserts document.documentElement.scrollWidth is at most 320.

K-003645.example: The spec sets the viewport to 320 by 568 and opens the modal from a button with data-testid open-modal. It expects the dialog boundingBox width to be at most 288px, which is 320 minus 2rem at a 16px root size.
K-003645.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and grep prints a line containing scrollWidth with a 320 comparison.
traps: A small model often checks only the dialog and skips the page scrollWidth, so horizontal overflow goes unnoticed.
Using 1280 by 800 as the only viewport proves nothing about phones.
Forgetting to wait for the dialog to be visible makes the measurement read a closed modal.

steps.do: Run the touch target Playwright spec that measures the close button.
Check the stylesheet sets min-height on the close button class.
Confirm the spec asserts boundingBox width and height are each at least 44.

K-003646.example: The spec opens the modal at 375 by 667 and reads the boundingBox of the element with aria-label Close dialog. It expects width 44 and height 44 or more, matching the 44px target size from WCAG 2.5.5.
K-003646.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and grep shows min-height: 44px in Modal.module.css.
traps: A small model may pick a 24px icon size and forget the padding that makes the hit area 44px.
Measuring the SVG icon instead of the button gives a false small number.
Setting min-height without min-width leaves narrow buttons below 44px.

steps.do: Search the modal stylesheet for max-height declarations.
Search the whole source tree for leftover 100vh values.
Lint the Modal component file to catch unused style imports.

K-003647.example: The stylesheet should contain max-height: 90dvh with a 100% fallback, and the 100vh search should return no lines in the modal files. A dvh unit tracks the visible viewport height as the mobile address bar moves.
K-003647.check: The first grep prints a line with 90dvh, the second grep prints nothing and exits with code 1, and eslint prints no errors.
traps: A small model may treat vh and dvh as the same and leave 100vh in place.
An empty grep result is the pass case here, so do not report it as a failure.
Setting max-height on the wrapper but not the scrolling content can push the footer off screen.

steps.do: Start the dev server if it is not already running.
Run axe against the modal demo route with the WCAG 2.1 AA tag set.
Confirm that dialog text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its background.

K-003648.example: The modal-demo route renders the dialog open by default, so axe scans it with the modal visible. Gray 595959 text on a white background reaches about 7 to 1, which passes the 4.5 to 1 minimum for normal text.
K-003648.check: axe prints 0 violations and lists passes for color-contrast and aria-dialog-name.
traps: Loading a page where the modal is still closed means axe checks an empty page and misses dialog rules.
A small model may skip the contrast number and assume the theme colors pass.
Axe does not check focus order, so a manual Tab test is still needed.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that tabs through the modal and checks focus stays inside.
Run the spec that closes the modal with Escape and checks focus returns to the opener button.
Confirm the component uses useRef to store the previously focused element.

K-003649.example: The trap spec presses Tab 12 times at 375 by 667 and expects document.activeElement to stay inside the dialog each time. The restore spec expects the button with data-testid open-modal to be focused within 200ms after Escape.
K-003649.check: Both Playwright runs print 1 passed, and grep prints a line containing useRef.
traps: A small model may test only with a mouse and never press Tab, so focus trapping goes untested.
Forgetting to store the opener element in a ref means focus lands on body after close.
Testing only at desktop width misses mobile layouts where the dialog covers different elements.

steps.do: Run the TypeScript compiler in no-emit mode across the project.
Lint the Modal component and its size map file.
Count the lines that declare breakpoint keys in the size map.

K-003650.example: The size map declares sm, md and lg breakpoints at 640px, 768px and 1024px, so the grep count should be 3 when each breakpoint sits on its own line. A prop like size={{ base: 'sm', md: 'lg' }} must type-check against the Breakpoint union.
K-003650.check: tsc prints nothing and exits 0, eslint reports 0 problems, and grep prints 3.
traps: A small model may run tsc with emit enabled and write build files into the repo.
Using plain string keys instead of the Breakpoint union hides typos like 'mdd'.
The count of 3 only holds if each breakpoint is declared on a single line.

steps.do: Confirm the dialog root has a role attribute of dialog in the source.
Confirm aria-modal is set to true on the same element.
Run the focus-trap Playwright spec that presses Tab 12 times and Shift+Tab 12 times.
Check the spec asserts document.activeElement stays inside the dialog after every key press.
Record the element index if the spec reports a focus leak, then fix the focus loop.

K-003651.example: Modal.tsx has role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" on the panel, so grep -c prints 1. The spec presses Tab 12 times on a modal with 3 focusable buttons and asserts focus never leaves the dialog.
K-003651.check: grep -c prints 1 and Playwright prints "1 passed" with no assertion errors.
traps: Adding aria-modal alone does not trap focus; the JavaScript focus loop still has to exist.
Small models often put the trap on the overlay div instead of the dialog panel.
Test Shift+Tab as well as Tab.

steps.do: Find where the trigger stores a ref used to restore focus on close.
Run the Escape-key Playwright spec filtered to the escape test name.
Check the spec asserts document.activeElement equals the trigger button after the modal closes.
Run the same spec five times to catch flaky focus timing.

K-003652.example: The modal opens from button#open-settings; the spec presses Escape and expects that button to have focus within 200ms. --repeat-each=5 runs the test five times.
K-003652.check: Playwright prints "5 passed" with no timeout errors.
traps: Focusing the trigger before the dialog unmounts can lose focus to body.
Restore focus after the close completes, such as in a requestAnimationFrame callback.
Run the spec repeatedly, because one pass can hide timing bugs.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173.
Open the modal state in the app by loading the route that renders it open.
Run axe against the open-modal route with WCAG 2 A and AA rule tags and exit on violations.
Read the summary and confirm there are no violation entries.

K-003653.example: The route /?modal=open renders the dialog open, and axe runs the wcag2a and wcag2aa rules against it. A clean scan exits with status 0.
K-003653.check: The axe command exits with status 0 and prints no violation entries for the modal.
traps: Scanning the closed page proves nothing about dialog labels or focus.
Axe does not check focus trapping, so pair it with the Playwright specs.
Dark-mode and reduced-motion states need their own scans.

steps.do: List the text color utilities used in the modal file.
Count uses of text-gray-300 and text-gray-400, which fail 4.5:1 on white.
Replace each match with text-gray-600 or darker on a bg-white surface.
Run the count again and confirm zero matches remain.

K-003654.example: Modal.tsx uses text-gray-400 on bg-white for helper text, about 2.5:1 contrast. After switching to text-gray-600, about 7.5:1 on white, the grep count is 0.
K-003654.check: The final grep -c prints 0 and the axe color-contrast rule reports no failures.
traps: Tailwind's text-gray-500 on white is about 4.8:1 and passes, but text-gray-400 does not.
Opacity utilities like text-black/50 lower contrast over a dark backdrop.
Measure the text against the actual background behind it, not just the class name.

steps.do: Confirm the close button sets size-11 in the source.
Run the Playwright bounding-box spec for the close button.
Check the spec reads boundingBox and expects width and height of at least 44.
Check the root font size is 16px so 2.75rem resolves to 44px.

K-003655.example: size-11 sets width and height to 2.75rem, which is 44px at the default 16px root font size. The spec reads boundingBox() and expects both values to be 44 or more.
K-003655.check: grep prints a line containing size-11 and Playwright prints "1 passed".
traps: size-10 is 40px and fails the 44px minimum.
Padding alone around a 16px icon can land below 44px.
Measure with boundingBox, not by eye.

steps.do: Confirm the dialog uses motion-reduce variants in the source.
Run the reduced-motion Playwright spec that emulates the reduce preference.
Check the spec sets reducedMotion to reduce in its emulation options.
Check the spec reads computed transitionDuration and expects 0s with reduce emulated.

K-003656.example: The dialog class includes motion-reduce:transition-none and motion-reduce:animate-none. With reducedMotion set to 'reduce', the spec reads getComputedStyle transitionDuration as 0s.
K-003656.check: grep prints a line containing motion-reduce:transition-none and Playwright prints "1 passed".
traps: motion-safe: applies only without the preference, so it cannot serve as the override.
Check computed style at runtime, not just the CSS source.
An unprefixed transition-none class will not be scoped to the reduce preference.

steps.do: Locate the CSS entry file that imports Tailwind.
Add the custom dark variant line directly after the tailwindcss import in that file.
Confirm the custom variant line appears exactly once in the entry file.
Build the stylesheet with the Tailwind v4 CLI.
Confirm the compiled CSS contains the dark selector.

K-003657.example: Add @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)); after @import 'tailwindcss'; so that dark:bg-slate-900 applies under any ancestor with class dark. The compiled output should contain one match for the selector, and the count command prints 1.
K-003657.check: The grep -c on the source prints 1 and the grep -c on dist/app.css prints 1 or more.
traps: Small models often keep the v3 darkMode key in tailwind.config.js, which v4 does not read. Do not use the prefers-color-scheme media default when the app uses a class toggle. Without the custom varia…

steps.do: List the select component directory to find the component file.
Replace the select class list with light color classes followed by dark: counterparts for border, background, and text.
Count the dark: variants in the select file to confirm each color has a dark pair.
Run the Playwright contrast spec that renders the select in light and dark themes.
Confirm the text on the dark background meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

K-003658.example: Use border-slate-300 bg-white text-slate-900 dark:border-slate-600 dark:bg-slate-900 dark:text-slate-100 on the select. Slate 100 text on slate 900 background is about 16:1, well above the 4.5:1 minimum.
K-003658.check: The grep prints 4 or more, and Playwright prints '2 passed' for the light and dark cases with no contrast failures.
traps: Small models often set only the light background and let dark text inherit an unreadable color. Keep each color utility paired with a dark: variant. Check the ratio is at least 4.5:1 for normal text,…

steps.do: Search the layouts for existing dark mode markers on the root element.
Add the scheme-dark utility to the select element so the browser renders its popup in dark colors.
Give each option element explicit dark background and text classes.
Confirm the compiled CSS includes the color-scheme declaration.
Run the Playwright dropdown test in dark mode.

K-003659.example: Write class='scheme-dark bg-slate-900 text-slate-100' on the select and class='bg-slate-900 text-slate-100' on each option. The compiled CSS should contain color-scheme: dark for the select.
K-003659.check: The grep count is 1 or more, and Playwright prints '1 passed' for the dark dropdown test.
traps: Small models often style the select box but forget scheme-dark, so the popup stays white. Dark classes on option elements alone do not set the popup's color-scheme. Do not rely on a global color-sche…

steps.do: Create the theme initialization script file in the public folder.
Write a script that reads the saved theme from localStorage and adds the dark class to the html element before first paint.
Find the line number of the script tag in index.html.
Find the line number of the body open tag and confirm the script line is smaller.
Run the Playwright test that checks for no light flash on reload.

K-003660.example: Place <script src='/theme-init.js'></script> in the head before the stylesheet link, with no defer or async attribute. The script line should print at a lower line number than the body tag.
K-003660.check: The script line number is lower than the body line number, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models often place the script after the body or add defer, which lets the light theme paint first. The script must run synchronously in the head. Wrap localStorage reads in a try block because …

steps.do: Install the Tailwind class sorting plugin for Prettier as a dev dependency.
Register the plugin in the Prettier config file so class names are sorted consistently.
Rewrite the select file with Prettier to sort its class names.
Check that the select file matches the Prettier style without changes.
Run the TypeScript compiler without emitting files to catch type errors in the component.

K-003661.example: After adding the plugin to the config as the plugins entry, the file rewrites its class list so dark: classes sort after base classes. Prettier then reports the file as already formatted.
K-003661.check: prettier --check prints 'All matched files use Prettier code style!' and tsc --noEmit exits with no output and code 0.
traps: Small models often build dark class names with string concatenation, such as 'dark:bg-' plus a variable, which Tailwind cannot detect. Write every full class name as a literal string. Sorting changes…

steps.do: Find the existing theme block in the CSS entry file.
Add --color-field: #ffffff inside the @theme block, then confirm the line exists.
Add a .dark selector that sets --color-field: #0f172a, then confirm the selector exists.
Build the stylesheet into dist/app.css.
Count lines that contain the variable in the built CSS. The count must be 2 or more: one for the root value and one for the dark override.
Confirm the select elements use the bg-field utility.

K-003662.example: Define --color-field: #ffffff in @theme and --color-field: #0f172a under .dark, then use class='bg-field' on the select. The build output should show the variable at least twice, once for the root and once for the dark override.
K-003662.check: rg -c prints a count of at least 2 for dist/app.css, and the component grep lists the select file with bg-field.
traps: Small models often write the override in a separate rule that is not scoped to .dark, so the dark value applies everywhere. Keep the token names identical in both places. Do not invent a utility name…

steps.do: Find the navigation timing budget written in the project docs.
Find any existing performance budget file in the project.
Record a 150ms show delay and a 200ms budget in PLAN.md.
Check that the show delay is below the budget.

K-003663.example: rg finds the line 'nav-ready under 200ms' in docs/perf.md. The plan sets showDelay to 150 so the bar stays hidden for a 40ms navigation.
K-003663.check: The test command exits with status 0 and prints nothing, and any nonzero status means the delay must be lowered.
traps: Small models show the bar at once, which causes flicker on fast navigations.
The delay must be shorter than the budget, not longer.
Do not invent a budget when the docs already state one.

steps.do: Find the layout load files that could return nav items.
Count label fields in existing nav fixture data.
Set the skeleton row count to the last known item count, capped between 3 and 7.
Check that the planned skeleton count of 5 is at least 3.

K-003664.example: The layout load returns 5 items, so the plan renders 5 rows with class nav-skeleton. The test command confirms 5 is at least 3.
K-003664.check: find prints the layout load path, rg prints a nonzero count, and test exits with status 0.
traps: Small models set the skeleton count equal to a long full list, which slows rendering.
Hardcoding 0 rows causes layout shift when items arrive.
Keep the count between 3 and 7.

steps.do: Count internal anchor lines in the navigation component.
Check whether any link already sets data-sveltekit-preload-data.
Set the policy to hover for nav links in PLAN.md and leave external links without the attribute.
Check that the internal nav anchor count of 8 is at most 10.

K-003665.example: rg reports 8 internal link lines in src/lib/Nav.svelte, and no preload-data attributes exist yet. The plan adds data-sveltekit-preload-data='hover' to those 8 anchors.
K-003665.check: rg prints a count of 8 or fewer, the preload-data search prints nothing before the change, and test exits with status 0.
traps: Small models add data-sveltekit-preload-data to external links, which SvelteKit ignores.
Setting it on a shared wrapper also preloads footer links, which adds requests.
Scope the attribute to the nav anchors only.

steps.do: Check whether an aria-live region already exists in the source tree.
Check whether aria-busy is already set on nav elements.
Record in PLAN.md that nav gets aria-busy true while navigating.to is set, and one role=status element announces Loading.
Confirm the axe-core package is published and print its latest version.

K-003666.example: rg finds no aria-live matches, so the plan adds one p element with role='status' and class sr-only in src/routes/+layout.svelte. npm view prints a semver string such as 4.10.2, which confirms axe-core is available for later checks.
K-003666.check: Both rg searches print nothing before the change, and npm view prints a version string in semver form such as 4.10.2.
traps: Small models put aria-live on the whole nav, which repeats announcements on every link.
Use one status element for the message.
Do not use role=alert for routine loading, because it interrupts the user.

steps.do: List all SvelteKit route pages under src/routes.
Count the internal nav anchors in the navigation component.
Check the SvelteKit version to choose the navigation store.
Run the Svelte type checker to confirm the project baseline and get an error count.
Create PLAN.md, then write the route count and store choice into it by hand.

K-003667.example: The find command lists 4 pages, such as src/routes/+page.svelte and src/routes/about/+page.svelte. The grep shows a 2.x version of @sveltejs/kit, and svelte-check reports 0 errors, so the plan uses navigating from '$app/state'.
K-003667.check: find prints exactly 4 paths, grep prints one line with @sveltejs/kit and a version starting with 2, and svelte-check prints a summary line with '0 errors'.
traps: Small models guess the route count instead of counting it.
They import navigating from $app/stores on SvelteKit 2.12 or later, where $app/state is the current module.
Do not edit source files during planning.

steps.do: Confirm each tabpanel exists with an id and an aria-labelledby attribute.
Start a local static server on port 8080 serving the site folder.
Run the Playwright spec that waits for aria-busy to change from true to absent on the panel.
Record the pass count and stop the server with Ctrl+C.

K-003668.example: Clicking the Reviews tab sets aria-busy="true" on #panel-reviews, and the spec asserts the attribute is gone within 2000ms of the fetch resolving. The run must print 1 passed.
K-003668.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the test log shows aria-busy absent on #panel-reviews after load.
traps: Small models often check aria-busy once instead of waiting for it to clear, so assert the removal with a 2000ms timeout.
Setting aria-busy on the tab button instead of the tabpanel is a common mistake, because the panel is the region that loads.

steps.do: Count skeleton elements in the source to get the starting number.
Start the local server on port 8080.
Run the spec that clicks the Specs tab and expects zero matches for .skeleton.
Confirm the starting count matched the number of skeleton blocks in the markup.

K-003669.example: tabs.html has 3 skeleton divs in the Specs panel, and after the click the spec expects locator('.skeleton').count() to equal 0. The grep must print 3 before the run.
K-003669.check: grep prints 3 and Playwright prints '1 passed' with the count assertion at 0.
traps: Counting skeletons immediately after the click returns 0 before the fetch starts, which passes falsely.
Wait for aria-busy to clear on the panel first, then count.

steps.do: Run Lighthouse performance audit against the running tabs page and save the JSON report.
Read the largest contentful paint value in milliseconds from the report.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the report.
Compare the LCP to 2500ms and the CLS to 0.1 and note any failure.

K-003670.example: The report returns an LCP of 1840.2 and a CLS of 0.04 after the Reviews panel loads lazily. Both values are under the thresholds of 2500ms and 0.1.
K-003670.check: The LCP command prints a number below 2500 and the CLS command prints a number below 0.1.
traps: LCP is reported in milliseconds, so 2500 means 2.5 seconds, not 2.5.
Pointing Lighthouse at a file path instead of an http URL skips the lazy-loaded panels and gives a false pass.

steps.do: Find the element that announces loading status to confirm role status is present.
Start the local server on port 8080.
Run the axe accessibility scan on the tabs page and exit with an error code if violations exist.
Check the loading message color pair against the 4.5:1 minimum and record the ratio.

K-003671.example: The text 'Loading reviews' uses #595959 on #ffffff, a contrast of 7.0:1, and the axe run reports zero violations. The role="status" element appears on line 42 of tabs.html.
K-003671.check: The grep prints a line number and the axe run reports 0 violations with exit code 0.
traps: A small model may accept a passing axe run without checking the loading text color ratio itself.
Verify each text color pair reaches at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

steps.do: Confirm the error container uses role alert and is in the tabpanel markup.
Run the Playwright spec that aborts the reviews request and expects the alert text within 1000ms.
Confirm the spec reports the alert became visible and the panel no longer has aria-busy.

K-003672.example: The spec routes /api/reviews to abort, and the alert 'Could not load reviews' must appear within 1000ms. The run must print 1 passed.
K-003672.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the alert locator reports visible within the timeout.
traps: Using role="status" for an error hides the failure from many screen readers, so use role="alert".
Forgetting to remove the route mock after the test leaks the abort into other tests.

steps.do: Find the keydown handler that handles ArrowRight and ArrowLeft in the tabs script.
Run the keyboard spec that holds the Reviews fetch open and presses ArrowRight.
Confirm the spec asserts aria-selected moves to the Specs tab within 200ms.

K-003673.example: While the Reviews fetch is held open, pressing ArrowRight moves aria-selected to the Specs tab within 200ms and moves focus with it. The reporter must list the test as passed.
K-003673.check: The grep prints a line number and Playwright lists the keyboard test as passed with a duration under 200ms.
traps: A small model may test only the click path and skip the keyboard path, which breaks when the handler waits on the fetch.
Keep the fetch pending in the test so the switch is tested during loading.

steps.do: Create the tests folder for the flicker test.
In app.py, call self.set_timer(0.2, self.show_loader) in on_mount and store the returned timer in self._loader_timer.
In show_loader, set the LoadingIndicator display to True only if the row list is still empty.
In the data-loaded handler, call self._loader_timer.stop() before hiding the indicator.
Create tests/test_flicker.py that loads data in 50ms and asserts the indicator is never displayed.
Run the flicker test.

K-003674.example: The data loads at 50ms, the timer is stopped, and the indicator never appears, so pytest reports one passing test.
K-003674.check: Output ends with '1 passed in' and contains no display assertion failure.
traps: Do not forget to stop the timer on load, or a spinner will appear over real data.
Use the float 0.2 for seconds; an integer delay will not match the 200ms spec.
Do not poll for load completion in a loop; rely on the message handler.

steps.do: Create the stylesheet file empty_state.tcss.
In empty_state.tcss, set #empty-box to width 50% and height auto, and set its parent container to align center middle.
Set CSS_PATH to empty_state.tcss on the App class so Textual loads the stylesheet.
Create tests/test_layout.py that runs the app at size 80 by 24 and reads the region of #empty-box.
Assert the region width is 40 cells and the region x offset is 20 cells.
Run the layout test.

K-003675.example: At 80 columns, width 50% gives 40 cells, and an x offset of (80 - 40) / 2 gives 20, so pytest reports one passing test.
K-003675.check: pytest prints '1 passed' with no AssertionError on region.width.
traps: Textual uses cells, not px, so write 50% or an integer cell count.
Pass size=(80, 24) to run_test; the default size will not check the minimum layout.
Make sure CSS_PATH matches the real location of empty_state.tcss.

steps.do: Read the svelte entries in package.json.
Check the installed svelte package version directly.
Confirm the svelte/motion module files are present in node_modules.
Note the major version in the plan and mark runes as available if the major version is 5 or higher.

K-003676.example: package.json lists svelte at 5.x, so the plan uses svelte/transition and svelte/motion with $state for values. npm ls svelte prints a single line for svelte at 5.x with no missing or invalid marks.
K-003676.check: npm ls svelte prints one version line with no missing or invalid marks, and ls lists the motion module files.
traps: Small models import from svelte/motion in a Svelte 4 project that expects stores. Read the version first.
Do not mix runes syntax into a file in a project pinned to an older Svelte major version.

steps.do: Search for any existing reduced-motion check in the source tree.
Decide the rule: when reduced motion is on, set every transition duration to 0 and drop fly movement.
Record the rule and the 200ms cap for normal motion in the motion plan file.
Confirm the plan names the fallback for every animated element.

K-003677.example: The plan says reduced motion sets duration to 0 for every fade and fly, with a 200ms cap otherwise. The search for prefers-reduced-motion returns 0 hits, so the check must be added to the onboarding components.
K-003677.check: rg -c prints a count equal to the number of animated elements in the table, and rg -n prefers-reduced-motion shows the match location once it is added.
traps: Small models write the fallback as a comment and never add the matchMedia query. Name the query and the element.
Do not set reduced-motion duration to a small nonzero value when the rule says 0.

steps.do: Find each loop over checklist items in the onboarding files.
Confirm each loop has a key expression in parentheses after the item name.
Plan animate:flip from svelte/animate with duration 150 on each keyed item.
Record the key field name and the 150ms duration in the motion plan.

K-003678.example: The checklist uses {#each items as item (item.id)} and the plan sets animate:flip with duration 150. The count of 150 in the plan file is 1 or more.
K-003678.check: rg -c 150 prints 1 or more, and the each search shows a block with a key such as (item.id) in parentheses.
traps: Small models leave out the key, so animate:flip does nothing. Use a stable key like item.id.
Do not use the array index as the key when items can move. Do not use a CSS transition on order instead of svelte/animate.

steps.do: Open the onboarding step list to see which steps exist.
Create the motion plan file.
Write a table header with columns for element, directive, and duration in ms.
Write one row per step: fade on the title with duration 200, and fly on the primary button with y 8 and duration 200. Use in and out for enter and leave.
Check that every row's total stays under a 300ms budget.
Confirm the file has one line per step plus the header line.

K-003679.example: Step 2 has a title and a button, so the plan says fade on the title for 200ms and fly on the button with y 8 for 200ms. Four steps give a count of 5 lines including the header.
K-003679.check: wc -l prints 5 for a four-step flow, matching the step count plus the header.
traps: Small models put transition on elements that are not mounted during the change, so nothing animates. Use in and out for enter and leave.
Import directives from svelte/transition, not from a generic animation library.

steps.do: Confirm the app sets document direction from the active i18next language using i18n.dir.
Run the RTL Playwright spec against the ar locale.
Check that the table's computed direction is rtl and the first header cell is aligned to the right edge.
Run the spec against he to confirm the same behavior for Hebrew.

K-003680.example: In src/i18n/index.ts, i18n.dir('ar') returns 'rtl', and the spec asserts getComputedStyle(table).direction equals 'rtl' with a 1rem cell padding on the start side. The ar run reports 2 passed for the direction and alignment assertions.
K-003680.check: The Playwright output shows '2 passed' for ar and he, and rg prints the line that calls i18n.dir.
traps: Using text-align: left or margin-left in CSS, which does not flip for RTL; use logical properties like text-align: start and padding-inline-start.
Setting dir on a wrapper div but not on the table, so nested tables render left-to-right.
Forgetting that sort icons and arrows must also be mirrored in RTL.

steps.do: Find every place the table formats a number or date to confirm it uses Intl and not toFixed or manual strings.
Run the unit test that renders the table in de-DE and checks the price cell text.
Check the Intl output directly in Node for the German grouping separator.

K-003681.example: The cell for price 1234.5 in de-DE shows '1.234,5', and the date 2026-11-04 shows '4.11.2026' through Intl.DateTimeFormat. The unit test asserts those two strings and passes.
K-003681.check: The Node command prints 1.234,5, and npm test reports the DataTable tests as passed with 0 failed.
traps: Calling toLocaleString() with no locale argument, which uses the machine locale and not the app language.
Formatting currency with a hardcoded symbol instead of Intl.NumberFormat with style: 'currency'.
